intended_object: The homomorphism G/ker(q) → F induced by a continuous homomorphism q : G → F from a profinite group to a discrete group, where ker(q) is open and normal so G/ker(q) is a finite quotient (first isomorphism theorem). Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `HomColimit.ofContinuousHom`.
explanation:
The body is Mathlib's `QuotientGroup.kerLift` applied to the homomorphism underlying q. That map sends the class of g to q(g), and it is well defined on the quotient by ker q. `kernelOpenNormal q` packages ker q as an open normal subgroup. Its underlying subgroup is definitionally `q.toMonoidHom.ker`, which is why the code type-checks. So the definition is exactly the induced map G/ker q → F that the docstring describes.

This is a thin wrapper and does not re-implement anything. The general construction is Mathlib's `kerLift`. The wrapper only fixes its domain to the quotient by the open normal subgroup `kernelOpenNormal q`, which the colimit construction needs as a stage index. Being specific to profinite groups and discrete targets is what makes the kernel open, so the special setting is part of what the definition is about; it is not an unnecessary restriction. It could also be seen as a helper for `HomColimit.ofContinuousHom`, but it does denote a standard object (the factorization through G/ker q), and it is correct.
